items.body:
**Feature request**

Please add settings in `config.toml` to control completion timestamps independently of elapsed work duration:

- Show or hide the completion timestamp.
- Choose automatic, 12-hour, or 24-hour formatting.
- Preserve the existing “Worked for…” duration when timestamps are hidden.

**Current behavior**

In Codex CLI **v0.156.1 on Linux**, successful responses display a completion timestamp. We could not find a configuration option to hide it.

My desktop clock uses 24-hour formatting, but Codex initially displayed:

```text
Worked for 1m 11s · 6:47 PM
```

Launching Codex with the following locale override successfully switched timestamps to 24-hour formatting:

```bash
env -u LC_ALL LC_TIME=C.UTF-8 codex
```

This works, but requires a launch command or shell alias. A dedicated display preference would avoid changing the locale inherited by child processes.

**Requested behavior**

Users should be able to choose between displays such as:

```text
Worked for 1m 11s
Worked for 1m 11s · 18:47
Worked for 1m 11s · 6:47 PM
```

When timestamps are hidden, short responses that do not qualify for “Worked for…” should show no completion-time footer. These preferences should apply consistently to new responses and restored conversation history.

**Related work**

- [#46845](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/46845) added clock-preference detection. This request adds explicit configuration and visibility controls.
- [#27203](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/27203) requests optional timestamps throughout CLI output. This request focuses specifically on the existing completion footer.

The relevant `/proc/self/mountinfo` entries have the same filesystem device and root:

```text
0:47 / /run/host/tmp ... - tmpfs tmpfs ...
0:47 / /tmp          ... - tmpfs tmpfs ...
```

`os.path.samefile("/tmp", "/run/host/tmp")` returns `True`.

Version comparison with the same container and command:

| Codex version | `codex sandbox -- pwd` |
| --- | --- |
| 0.153.4 | succeeds |
| 0.154.0 | succeeds |
| 0.155.1 | succeeds |
| 0.156.1 | fails with the error above |

I did not have a 0.156.0 binary available to test, so the observed regression boundary is between 0.155.1 and 0.156.1.

### What is the expected behavior?

The filesystem-restricted sandbox should preserve app-server socket isolation and execute `pwd` under this standard Toolbx mount layout, as 0.155.1 did.

items.title: Fix no-reparse directory opens on Windows 10
items.body:
Fix no-reparse directory opens on Windows 10

## Why

Windows 10 rejects the Object Manager drive-letter link when opening a directory with `OBJ_DONT_REPARSE`, preventing ordinary local-drive paths from opening successfully.

## What changed

Resolve drive-letter aliases with `QueryDosDeviceW` before calling `NtCreateFile`. Accept only direct disk-volume mappings, rejecting other devices and volume subpaths. Leave filesystem components unresolved so `OBJ_DONT_REPARSE` continues to reject filesystem reparse points.

## Testing

Add tests for drive-root opens and NT path construction using ordinary and verbatim drive paths, plus validation of accepted disk-volume mappings and rejected device or subpath mappings.

Expose tool dispatch and timing observations to extensions

items.title: Realtime delegation repeats the user's utterance in <input> and <transcript_delta>

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: agent
labels.description: Issues related to the core agent loop

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

In `codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs`, `realtime_delegation_from_handoff` renders
`RealtimeDelegation { input: input_transcript, transcript_delta: realtime_transcript_delta(active_transcript) }`.
`realtime_transcript_delta` joins every `active_transcript` entry verbatim, and the final `user:` entry is usually the same utterance as `input_transcript`. So each delegation carries the user's request twice, once in `<input>` and again as the last `user:` line of `<transcript_delta>`. That wastes tokens on every handoff.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start a realtime (voice) conversation that delegates to the agent.
2. Say one request that triggers a handoff.
3. Inspect the rendered `<realtime_delegation>`. The final `user:` line of `<transcript_delta>` repeats the text of `<input>`.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the last transcript entry has role `user` and the whitespace-normalized `input` already contains its text, omit that entry from `<transcript_delta>`. Keep it when it adds words that the input lacks, so no context is lost. This is about 10 lines plus two tests. items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (`codex cloud`, checked through 0.156.1) and Codex Cloud on the web

### What feature would you like to see?

Two gaps keep Codex Cloud from hosting an unattended, stateful agent workflow: an agent that works in short sessions, keeps its state in the repository, decides when its next session should start, and occasionally waits for a human reply.

**1. Per-task model and reasoning effort for cloud tasks**

`codex cloud exec` can't choose the model or reasoning effort for a task. The request it sends carries only the environment, branch, QA mode, input and number of attempts. Local `codex exec` supports `--model` and `-c model_reasoning_effort=...`. The same controls for cloud tasks would let a workflow use a lighter setting for routine runs and a stronger one for deep work:

```bash
codex cloud exec --env ENV_ID --model MODEL --reasoning-effort LEVEL "..."
```

**2. Scheduled cloud tasks bound to an environment and branch**

Scheduled tasks can run in the desktop app, but only while the computer is on. They can also run on the web, but there they can't target a repository environment. Nothing schedules a Codex Cloud task, in a configured environment and branch, for a future time or a recurrence. Something like:

```bash
codex cloud schedule --env ENV_ID --branch main --at 2026-09-30T10:00 --timezone America/New_York "..."
codex cloud schedule --env ENV_ID --branch main --cron "0 10 * * 6" --timezone America/New_York "..."
codex cloud schedule list --json
codex cloud schedule cancel SCHEDULE_ID
```

Being able to create a schedule from inside a running cloud task would let an agent book its own next run.

### Additional information

The third piece is continuing an existing task by ID, such as `codex cloud message TASK_ID "..."`. That is already requested in #24777, so I've 👍'd it there instead of repeating it.

This workflow runs today with local `codex exec`, `codex exec resume` and an external scheduler. It can't move to Codex Cloud until cloud tasks can be scheduled, can choose their model and effort, and can be continued.

Related:
- #24777: scriptable environment and task lifecycle, including messaging an existing task
- #42970: model selection in Codex Cloud from the mobile app

items.body:
## Summary

Codex can see network failures in its restricted command environment while the user's shell can reach GitHub normally. During a requested PR review, `gh pr view` and `git ls-remote` run through Codex's restricted command path failed to connect/resolve GitHub. The user ran `git ls-remote` in their shell and it succeeded. Codex then treated its own command-environment failure as inability to verify the PR head, instead of clearly distinguishing the two environments and retrying through an available authorized path.

The user reports that their own GitHub commands have been succeeding while Codex's commands have failed repeatedly. This report concerns Codex's handling of that mismatch, not a claim that GitHub DNS was down for the user.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a Codex session with restricted command networking, ask for a review of a GitHub PR at its current head.
2. Run a read-only GitHub check such as `gh pr view <number>` or `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<number>/head` through the restricted command path.
3. Observe the command fail with a DNS or connection error.
4. Run `git ls-remote` in the user's normal shell and observe it succeed.
5. Observe Codex stop at its own environment's failure rather than clearly report the execution-context difference and retry through an available authorized route.

## Expected behavior

Codex should distinguish command-sandbox network failures from the user's host/network state. When a requested verification is blocked in the restricted environment, it should explain that scope and, if an authorized path is available, retry the read-only check through it. It should not characterize the user's DNS/network as unavailable based only on failures in Codex's restricted command environment.

## Actual behavior

The restricted Codex command path failed to reach GitHub, while the user's shell command succeeded. Codex stopped verification and told the user it could not confirm the PR head, requiring the user to run and paste a routine Git command.

## Additional context

There are existing reports about DNS failures in specific Codex environments, including #16782. This report focuses on the agent's failure to distinguish its restricted command environment from a working user shell and to use an available authorized verification path.

No Codex version or app build was captured during this session.

items.title: Make Linux descriptor cleanup fork-safe
items.body:
Make Linux descriptor cleanup fork-safe

## Why

Linux descriptor cleanup used allocating directory enumeration after `fork`. The child needs allocation-free cleanup while preserving Rust's spawn-error channel until `exec` succeeds.

## What changed

- Mark unrelated descriptors close-on-exec with `close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`, leaving stdio and explicitly preserved descriptors' flags untouched.
- Fall back to stack-backed `getdents64` enumeration of the child's descriptor table when `close_range` fails.
- Document best-effort cleanup: failures allow launch to proceed and may leave unrelated descriptors inherited.

## Testing

Add Linux tests for descriptor inheritance, unsorted and duplicate allowlists, unchanged parent descriptors, fallback cleanup above a lowered descriptor limit, preserved exec-error reporting, and successful launch when both cleanup paths fail. Retain MCP coverage for descriptor exclusion in servers and descendants.

items.title: Attach inherited rollout history to diagnostic reports
items.body:
Attach inherited rollout history to diagnostic reports

## Why

Selected rollouts can reference history stored in ancestor rollouts through `history_base`. Attaching only the selected files leaves that inherited history out of diagnostic reports.

## What changed

When `include_logs` is enabled, follow nested `history_base` references and attach ancestor prefixes up to the recorded byte offsets. Deduplicate ancestors, retain the largest requested prefix, and skip rollouts already selected for upload.

Bound discovery to 64 ancestors and five seconds, and enforce attachment size limits. Missing, unreadable, or incomplete ancestor prefixes are best effort and do not prevent the report upload.

## Testing

Add a unit test verifying that nested parent and grandparent history bases are attached with the expected filenames and contents.

### What feature would you like to see?

Add a first-class, hard tool allowlist that restricts every callable tool source for a session. For CLI, a project or user configuration could look like:

```toml
[tools]
allowed_tools = ["exec_command", "write_stdin"]
```

When present, this must affect model-visible and executable tools alike, including built-in tools (`apply_patch`, shell/code-mode tools, `request_user_input`), collaboration tools, hosted tools, MCP tools, extensions/apps, dynamic tools, and tool discovery. The allowlist should compose with host policy and sandbox/approval settings: it may only remove access, never grant it. An empty list should intentionally expose no tools; omitting the setting preserves today's behavior.

Namespaced tools should be selectable unambiguously, for example `collaboration.wait_agent`; bare names can mean the default `functions` namespace. Generated code-mode tools must require explicit inclusion too.

### Additional information

Today the documented controls are scoped: MCP `enabled_tools` applies to an MCP server, app tool settings apply to an app, and feature flags can disable selected capabilities. They do not provide a complete session-wide boundary.

This is needed for constrained workflows and security-sensitive integrations where the caller must be able to start Codex with exactly a known tool set. Tool visibility is not enough: denied tools must also be impossible to execute.

I searched the issue tracker for `allowed_tools`, `tool allowlist`, and `restrict tools` before filing. A local proof-of-concept branch exists, but I understand the project does not accept external pull requests.

This is an implementation proposal related to #21653 (multiple status-line rows) and the horizontal-spacing aspect of #27279 (status-line padding).

The existing ordered `tui.status_line` list gains two repeatable layout entries:

- `line-break` starts another status-line row.
- `space` adds one space of leading indentation or replaces the default separator between fields; repeated entries widen the gap.

Users can arrange fields across rows and control their order and spacing. The `/statusline` picker supports repeated layout entries and previews multiple rows. Existing configurations retain their behavior.

```toml
[tui]
status_line = [
  "model", "space", "space", "reasoning",
  "line-break",
  "current-dir", "git-branch",
  "line-break",
  "context-remaining", "five-hour-limit",
]
```

The implementation includes rendering and picker coverage, including snapshots, constrained terminal sizes, and hyperlinks on later rows. Each configured row truncates independently to the terminal width. Automatic wrapping based on terminal width and vertical padding above/below the footer are outside this proposal’s scope.

The PR is open and ready for review on my fork. Creating a PR directly against `openai/codex` was rejected: upstream currently restricts PR creation to collaborators, and my account has read access. items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.156.1`. The problem also reproduces with 0.156.0; 0.155.1 and earlier tested versions work.

### What subscription do you have?

N/A. This reproduces locally with `codex sandbox -- /bin/true` before any model request.

### Which model were you using?

N/A.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.4.0 x86_64, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP6 on an HPE Cray HPC login node. `bubblewrap 0.11.0` is installed at `/usr/bin/bwrap`.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

SSH terminal; not terminal-dependent.

### Codex doctor report

`codex doctor` reports Codex 0.156.1, a consistent standalone installation, and the restricted Linux filesystem sandbox. The persistent app-server is not running. The only relevant processes in the reproducing session are `codex resume` and its 0.156.1 `codex-code-mode-host` child.

### What issue are you seeing?

Starting in 0.156.0, every filesystem-restricted command fails before bubblewrap starts when `/tmp` is isolated per user by `pam_namespace`:

```text
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /cray/tmp; remove the bind-mount alias or nested mount before starting the sandbox
```

The system's `/etc/security/namespace.conf` contains:

```text
/tmp    /tmp/.pam_namespace/    user    root
```

The resulting relevant mountinfo entries, with the username redacted, are:

```text
37227 37226 0:52 / /cray/tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:2 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
37229 37226 0:52 /tmp /tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:3 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
37462 37229 0:52 /tmp/.pam_namespace/<user> /tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:3 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
```

Thus `/cray/tmp` is the root of the tmpfs, `/tmp` is a view of its `/tmp` subtree, and the per-user PAM namespace directory is stacked back over `/tmp`. The PAM namespace parent is root-owned and mode `000`, so the physical-looking alias beneath `/cray/tmp/tmp/.pam_namespace/<user>` is not traversable by the user.

Codex creates `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>` with mode 0700. A filesystem-only trace of the 0.156.1 sandbox helper shows:

```text
readlink("/tmp", ...) = -1 EINVAL
mkdir("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", 0700) = -1 EEXIST
lstat("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", {st_mode=S_IFDIR|0700, ...}) = 0
open("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = 3
open("/proc/self/mountinfo", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 4
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /cray/tmp; ...
```

This is a Codex preflight rejection; bubblewrap itself is not reached.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a Linux login session configured with the `pam_namespace` entry above:

```bash
codex sandbox -- /bin/true
```

Regression results using locally cached standalone binaries on the same host:

```text
0.139.0  succeeds
0.146.1  succeeds
0.155.1  succeeds
0.156.0  fails with the /cray/tmp error
0.156.1  fails with the /cray/tmp error
```

The boundary corresponds to #45984, which added app-server Unix-socket isolation in 0.156.0. This appears related to #47455, but that report uses a fully overmounted `nix-user-chroot` mount. This report covers standard PAM per-user namespace mounts, where the alternate physical path is also inaccessible through a root-owned mode-000 ancestor.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should preserve app-server socket isolation while allowing filesystem-restricted commands under a standard `pam_namespace` private `/tmp` configuration.

### Additional information

Attempted mitigations:

- Setting `TMPDIR=/run/user/<uid>` or to a workspace directory does not help. The sandbox helper still opens `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>`.
- `--no-daemon` does not avoid the validation.
- `features.use_legacy_landlock=true` is not a fallback; it panics with `filesystem-restricted execution requires bubblewrap to isolate app-server sockets`.
- Approved unsandboxed execution works.
- Downgrading to 0.155.1 restores sandbox execution, but that predates the socket-isolation security fix and is not a desirable permanent workaround.

No mounts, PAM configuration, or system security settings were modified during diagnosis.

Classify retryable exec-server preparation errors by type

## Why

Transient connection and registry failures can reach remote filesystem callers as generic `io::ErrorKind::Other` errors. Callers need a typed signal to identify failures that read-only preparation can retry.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
ChatGPT-issued:

---

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Codex Desktop client version `26.917.62051` (official Linux app).

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64, KDE Plasma/X11.

### What issue are you seeing?

When the per-user Linux inotify instance quota (`fs.inotify.max_user_instances`) is exhausted, Codex Desktop fails very poorly:

- new local tasks remain indefinitely on **"Starting your task"**
- existing Codex threads may stop loading
- Codex CLI continues to work normally
- the local app-server can still initialize and answer ordinary RPCs
- the Desktop UI does not surface any actionable error

The app logs do contain the actual low-level failure:

```text
inotify_init1() failed: Too many open files (24)
```

but the visible failure mode looks like auth/session/app-server corruption rather than inotify exhaustion.

This is **not** ordinary per-process file-descriptor exhaustion.

At the time of reproduction:

```text
ChatGPT open_fds = 290
Max open files = 1048576 / 1048576
system file-nr = 35872
fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 128
```

The user session had many inotify instances spread across VS Code, KDE, Electron apps, etc. Codex Desktop itself only held a few, but once the per-UID instance quota was exhausted, further `inotify_init1()` calls failed.

### Immediate workaround / strong causal evidence

Running:

```bash
sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024
```

immediately restored:

- loading existing Codex threads
- starting new local tasks

No app reinstall, auth reset, profile reset, or reboot was required.

### Additional isolation performed

- `codex exec ...` worked while Desktop was broken.
- The Desktop-bundled app-server initialized successfully and serviced config/auth RPCs.
- A clean Chromium profile via a separate `--user-data-dir` helped transiently, but the problem returned.
- Before raising the inotify limit, the Desktop logs repeatedly showed:
  ```text
  inotify_init1() failed: Too many open files (24)
  ```
- After raising `fs.inotify.max_user_instances`, the failure disappeared immediately.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux, set or retain a relatively low per-user inotify instance limit, e.g.:
   ```bash
   sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_instances
   # 128
   ```
2. Consume the per-user inotify instance quota with other desktop applications/processes.
3. Launch Codex Desktop.
4. Try to open existing Codex threads and/or start a new local task.

### Actual behavior

Codex Desktop can hang indefinitely on **"Starting your task"**, and existing thread history may fail to load, while the CLI and app-server remain otherwise functional.

The only useful indication is buried in stderr/log output:

```text
inotify_init1() failed: Too many open files (24)
```

### Expected behavior

At minimum, Codex Desktop should detect `inotify_init1() == -1` with `errno=EMFILE` and surface an actionable diagnostic indicating that the per-user inotify instance limit may be exhausted.

Ideally, subsystems that do not strictly require filesystem watching should degrade gracefully rather than making task startup/thread loading fail silently.

### Related but not duplicates

- #40940 — same visible "Starting your task" symptom on Linux, but reports AppServerManager RPC disconnects rather than inotify quota exhaustion.
- #37971 / #26984 — `EMFILE` from ordinary file-descriptor exhaustion/leaks, not `fs.inotify.max_user_instances`.

The distinction matters because raising `RLIMIT_NOFILE` does not fix this case; raising `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` does.

### Codex App version

26.917.51856, build 10492 (read from the installed application's Info.plist).

### Subscription

The specific subscription tier was not collected during diagnosis.

### Platform

macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon / arm64 (checked using sw_vers and uname).
Proxy application: Clash Verge.

### What issue are you seeing?

Previously, I only needed to enable the macOS system proxy when opening the application. After the app opened, I could disable the system proxy and still send messages and receive responses. I have proxy environment variables, including HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY, configured in ~/.codex/.env.

Now, after disabling the system proxy, clicking Send leaves the send button spinning indefinitely and the message cannot be submitted normally. Sending and receiving messages works with the system proxy enabled.

This is an observed change in behavior. The first affected app version is unknown, and no comparison with an older version has been performed to identify the update that introduced it.

### Steps to reproduce (observed during normal use)

1. Keep the proxy service running and configure proxy environment variables in ~/.codex/.env.
2. Enable the macOS system proxy and open the app.
3. After startup, disable the system proxy setting only.
4. Enter a message and click Send.
5. The send button keeps spinning and the message cannot be sent normally.
6. For comparison, messages can be sent and responses received with the system proxy enabled.

### Diagnostics performed

- A TCP connection to the HTTP proxy endpoint configured in .env succeeded.
- An unauthenticated HEAD request using curl with that HTTP proxy explicitly selected reached https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage and returned HTTP 405. This only establishes HTTP reachability; it does not verify authenticated requests or WebSocket connectivity.
- The same request with proxying explicitly disabled timed out after approximately 5 seconds, with HTTP status 000.
- Explicitly selecting the HTTP proxy endpoint used by the current system proxy configuration also returned HTTP 405.
- Recent desktop logs contain net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT for multiple routes, including /wham/usage, /settings/user, /sentinel/heartbeat, and /celsius/ws/user.
- These log entries have not been precisely correlated with a particular failed Send attempt, so they do not establish which request causes the submission to hang.

Redacted error excerpt:

```text
sa_server_request_failed
errorMessage=net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT
routePattern=/wham/usage
```

### Additional configuration observation and limitations

ALL_PROXY / all_proxy in .env point to a separate SOCKS port, which returned Connection refused during inspection. The HTTP port configured in HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY was reachable. The SOCKS configuration has not yet been corrected and tested independently, so this factor has not been ruled out.

During diagnosis, no system proxy settings were toggled, no configuration was changed, and the app was not restarted for a controlled reproduction. The enabled/disabled system proxy comparison above comes from my observations during normal use.

One hypothesis is that some desktop requests use a different proxy configuration path from the backend. This remains unconfirmed; this report does not establish that the current version entirely ignores .env.

### Expected behavior / questions

1. Which desktop and backend requests are covered by proxy settings in ~/.codex/.env? Has the current version changed proxy handling for requests required before message submission or for real-time connections?
2. If a network request fails or a submission prerequisite cannot complete, the app should show an actionable error and allow retrying instead of leaving the send button spinning indefinitely.
3. What additional diagnostics would help identify the failing request? Is there an app-level proxy configuration that covers these requests without requiring the system proxy to remain enabled?

### Related reports

I searched for existing reports but did not find one with the same platform, version, and trigger conditions:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/13682 — macOS + Clash Verge, different proxy behavior between the GUI and CLI, but different system proxy trigger conditions.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46824 — a send button that spins indefinitely, but on Windows and without an established link to proxy settings.

No raw logs, conversation content, account information, machine-specific absolute paths, or actual proxy addresses are attached.

2. During an already-running normal user turn in the desktop task, the exact hook definition was reviewed and trusted through the supported CLI hook-review UI. The CLI reported the conversation was open in another app and was exited without submitting a model prompt or transferring the task.
3. A separate read-only app-server process using the same backend binary returned the definition as enabled and trusted, with no hook-discovery errors. This was not a read of the active desktop task's in-memory hook registry.
4. The active desktop process's own runtime log for the test turn included `CodexHooks` in its enabled feature list.
5. The turn emitted its planned final reply and completed. The retrieved task history contained no matching hook event or corrective continuation. The command's invocation log had no entry for that turn; it contained only the earlier manual test. No continuation reservation was created.
6. A separate scheduled fallback later collected the result. The test itself was not a scheduled turn. The pilot is now disabled and has not been repeated.

## Expected behavior and limits

The intended behavior was invocation of the trusted Stop command, followed by a continuation request if its check failed. It is unknown whether activation during an already-running turn should take effect before that turn ends. No error specific to this hook was found in the retrieved history or retained hook-component logs. Absence from those records does not prove that every internal action was logged.

This report does not claim that all desktop hooks are unsupported, that a platform defect has been established, or that Stop can prevent the original assistant text from appearing.

## Requested clarification

1. Are project Stop definitions and trust loaded at session start, turn start, or dynamically? What supported action refreshes them in an existing desktop task?
2. What supported diagnostic interface shows the active task's registered Stop hooks and any reason a handler was skipped?
3. Is any supported mechanism guaranteed to withhold assistant text before display, or does Stop only request a subsequent continuation?

Please provide a supported activation/inspection procedure or confirm the applicable limitation. The goal is to establish the integration boundary before conducting any additional live test.

## Why

Pipe spawning installs Unix `pre_exec` hooks, forcing a fork on macOS even though the shared child launcher supports native spawning.

## Testing

Add macOS integration coverage verifying fork avoidance, executable path lookup, pipe I/O, session isolation, and descriptor inheritance. Add Unix regression tests for pipe and PTY fallback under descriptor pressure and for rejecting NUL inputs without running the child.

- Windows OpenSSH: `9.5p2`
- Remote login shell: Git Bash

## Problem

Opening an existing task in an SSH-backed remote project causes two to four console windows to flash before any prompt is sent or any model turn starts. In one reproduction, a visible `C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe` window remained open. The remote host can still become healthy and show a green status indicator, but the visible windows make the multi-account remote-project workflow disruptive.

## Reproduction

1. On Windows, configure a concrete SSH alias pointing to a loopback-only Windows OpenSSH server.
2. Use `SetEnv CODEX_HOME=...` to isolate a second Codex account.
3. Add a remote project in the Desktop app using that SSH alias.
4. Create or open an existing task in that remote project.
5. Restart the Desktop app, then open the existing remote task without sending a message.

## Expected

SSH discovery, login-shell startup, and `codex app-server proxy` should run fully in the background with no visible console windows.

## Actual

Console windows flash during the cold SSH connection. The behavior happens before model inference and does not require running a task command.

Observed process chains:

```text
ChatGPT.exe -> C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe -> conhost.exe
sshd.exe -> C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe -> conhost.exe
```

The Desktop process starts SSH with arguments similar to:

```text
ssh.exe -T -v -o BatchMode=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=12 <alias> ... codex app-server proxy
```

## Additional findings

- Updating the profile-managed App Server from `0.155.1` to `0.156.1` did not eliminate the windows.
- Recreating a project card would still use the same SSH alias and login shell.
- The current production Desktop build reports as up to date.
- Account authorization, sessions, project files, and separate `CODEX_HOME` directories remain intact.
- Local wrapper workarounds were tested and fully rolled back because they affected another SSH host. The system is back on the stock Windows OpenSSH client and Git Bash default shell.

No credentials, account identifiers, session contents, or API keys are included. Screenshots are available if maintainers need them.

items.title: Stream daemon executable hashing off the async runtime
items.body:
Stream daemon executable hashing off the async runtime

## Why

Debug executables can be hundreds of megabytes. Computing their identity previously loaded the entire file into memory and hashed it on an async runtime thread.

## What changed

Stream executable contents into the BLAKE3 hasher using `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, preserving the existing digest format while avoiding whole-file allocation and moving hashing off the async runtime.

items.title: Keep unfinished link destinations out of rich streaming previews
items.body:
Keep unfinished link destinations out of rich streaming previews

## Why

An unfinished Markdown link can display its destination across multiple preview rows, then collapse when the closing parenthesis arrives.

## What changed

Keep the link label visible while withholding the opening parenthesis and destination until the link closes. Scan incoming text incrementally, accounting for nested parentheses, escapes, angle-bracket destinations, titles, and inline code. Apply this holdback only to rich prose previews; newline commitment and finalization still render the original source.

## Testing

Add regression tests for character-by-character input, long Unicode destinations, resizing, raw-mode switching, and flushing unfinished links on newline or completion, plus a snapshot of the label-only preview.

## Summary

On Windows, the desktop app no longer shows existing ChatGPT Projects in the dedicated **Projects** section, even though the projects still exist server-side and remain visible through other surfaces.

Separately, `codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe` continues running after the desktop app is fully exited and blocks Windows app maintenance operations such as Update, Repair, and Reset until it is manually terminated.

This appears to have started after the PC crashed or was powered off unexpectedly.

Related / possibly overlapping issue: #39121

## Environment

- Windows desktop app
- Reproduced with both the current and previous app version
- ChatGPT web app shows the affected projects correctly
- Exact app build not recorded yet

## Issue 1: Projects missing from Windows desktop app

Existing ChatGPT projects are no longer shown in the **Projects** section of the Windows desktop app.

The projects themselves have not been deleted:

- On chatgpt.com, all affected projects are still visible under **Projects**.
- On chatgpt.com, they are also visible under **Pinned**.
- In the Windows app, the same projects are still accessible through **ChatGPT → Pinned**.
- Chats that belong to those projects still display their project assignment.
- Search results still show the project assignment of affected chats.
- Only the actual **Projects** list in the Windows desktop app is missing/empty.

### Expected behavior

The Windows desktop app should show the same existing project structure that is visible on chatgpt.com.

### Actual behavior

The project data still exists and can be referenced through chats and Pinned items, but the dedicated Projects view in the Windows desktop app does not display the projects.

## Troubleshooting already performed

The following did not fix the issue:

- Updating the desktop app
- Signing out and signing back in
- Multiple Windows restarts
- Uninstalling and reinstalling the desktop app
- Windows App Repair
- Windows App Reset
- Repeating Reset after manually terminating the Codex sandbox service
- Temporarily moving/resetting `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`
- Temporarily moving/resetting `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex`

The web application continues to display the projects correctly throughout these tests.

## Issue 2: codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe does not terminate with the app

When the desktop app is fully exited, `codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe` continues running.

This prevents Windows app-management operations such as:

- Update
- Repair
- Reset

The process/service has to be terminated manually before those operations can complete.

This behavior was reproduced with both the current and previous desktop-app version.

## Additional observation

Temporarily moving/resetting the `.codex` directory causes locally displayed Codex conversation history to disappear until the original `.codex` data is restored, indicating that at least part of Codex history/state is local.

This appears separate from the missing ChatGPT Projects problem, because the Projects issue persists after reinstall/reset while the same projects remain fully visible on the web.

## Summary

There appear to be two potentially related Windows desktop-app issues:

1. The app stops rendering/indexing existing ChatGPT Projects even though the server-side project structure remains intact and can still be observed through the web app, Pinned items, chat metadata, and search.
2. The Codex sandbox service survives a complete app exit and blocks app maintenance operations until manually terminated.

No project data appears to have been lost server-side.

A user can reply to a streamed question before its completed message is recorded. Assigning the assistant message's order at completion can place the reply before the question in retained context.

items.title: Retain assistant context for Guardian authorization reviews
items.body:
Retain assistant context for Guardian authorization reviews

## Why

Ordinary user replies can depend on preceding assistant messages. Losing those messages during compaction can leave Guardian without the context needed to interpret a reply's scope.

## What changed

- Retain original assistant messages, including commentary, with their recorded order across checkpoints and resume. Exclude compaction output from this evidence.
- Include assistant context in local and delegated reviews as untrusted context, with separate storage limits and lower budget priority than user instructions.
- Prefer assistant context preceding ordinary replies when selecting bounded root evidence, and report unavailable context without inferring what a reply refers to.
- Preserve inherited context scope and remove assistant evidence beyond rollback boundaries, including during rollout migration.

## Testing

Extend coverage for compaction and resume, checkpoint migration, queued-input ordering and rollback, role labeling, and evidence budgets that preserve user restrictions while dropping assistant context.

items.title: macOS: interactive codex CLI sessions never reap SkyComputerUseClient helpers; count grows per turn with session age

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Interactive `codex` CLI sessions on macOS leave `SkyComputerUseClient` helper processes running after each turn. Each turn spawns new helpers (an `mcp` helper, plus an `event-stream` helper in the samples I caught) as children of the `codex` process, and the earlier ones are never reaped. So the helper count grows with how long a session has been open, and total resident memory grows with it.

This looks related to #43471 (idle desktop app-server leaking helper pairs) and #29157 (leaked `turn-ended` helpers). The difference here is the surface: long-lived interactive CLI sessions, where the growth follows turns, not a timer.

## Environment

- `codex-cli 0.156.1`, interactive sessions (not the desktop app-server)
- macOS 26.6.2, arm64, 48 GB RAM
- Computer Use bundle installed at `~/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app`
- Several `codex` sessions open at once, each running for days

## Reproduction

1. Start an interactive `codex` session with Computer Use installed.
2. Run turns as normal. Computer Use itself doesn't need to be invoked.
3. Watch the helper count per parent session:

```bash
ps -Ao pid,ppid,rss,command | grep '[S]kyComputerUseClient' \
  | awk '{n[$2]++; r[$2]+=$3} END{for(p in n) print p, n[p], int(r[p]/1024)" MB"}'
ps -o pid,etime,comm -p <parent-pid>
```

## Observed

Snapshot of one machine, one row per live `codex` session (session age, then helpers still alive, then their combined RSS):

| session age | helpers | helper RSS |
|---|---|---|
| 8d 15h | 81 | 789 MB |
| 4d 12h | 6 | 192 MB |
| 4d 10h | 4 | 146 MB |
| 22h | 12 | 383 MB |
| 19h | 12 | 399 MB |
| 17h | 14 | 443 MB |
| 2 min | 2 | 75 MB |

- 154 helpers alive across 13 sessions, about 3 GB RSS combined. Each helper is roughly 30 to 40 MB.
- A brand-new session starts with 2 helpers, so the growth comes from turns.
- Earlier the same machine reached **377** helpers and about **8 GB** of helper RSS. Swap hit 8.7 of 10.2 GB, load average passed 190, and the machine was effectively stalled until the sessions were restarted.
- Helper parents are the `codex` CLI processes themselves, not `launchd`.

## Expected

Once a turn ends, its helpers should exit (or be reused), so helper count stays bounded no matter how old the session is.

## Workaround

Restarting a long-lived `codex` session frees its helpers. For now we monitor the helper count and restart sessions that pass a threshold.

Personal ChatGPT account — prefer not to disclose exact tier publicly

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200, build 26200, x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop Browser Use blocks read-only access to AliExpress even after the user manually signs in through the built-in browser and explicitly asks Codex to check the status of their most recent order.

Browser Use rejects the request before inspecting the page:

> Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The site-safety policy blocks this action; no user permission prompt or Auto-review was attempted. Browser use is not permitted on https://de.aliexpress.com.

No permission prompt or appeal option is presented. Codex cannot read even the order status although the user is signed in and has explicitly authorized this read-only task.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open https://de.aliexpress.com/?gatewayAdapt=glo2deu manually in the built-in browser.
2. Sign in to an existing AliExpress account.
3. Confirm that the AliExpress page is accessible manually.
4. Ask Codex to check the status of the most recent order.
5. Codex attempts to access the already-open browser tab.
6. Browser Use rejects the request before reading the page with the site-safety policy error quoted above.

### What is the expected behavior?

For an explicitly authorized and supervised read-only task, Browser Use should allow access after user approval, present a permission request, or explain the precise policy source, scope, duration, and available appeal procedure.

### Additional information

A local configuration check found no AliExpress-specific deny rule. No local managed_config.toml or Windows system requirements.toml was present.

Impact: the restriction prevents legitimate use of Codex to inspect the user’s own order status. Manually copying information or supplying screenshots defeats the purpose of supervised browser assistance.

Requested action: please investigate whether AliExpress is intentionally blocked by a service-side policy or affected by a policy-classification bug. Please permit user-approved read-only access, provide a visible approval or appeal mechanism, or document the restriction and its precise reason.

No passwords, payment details, or order information are included in this report.
